display.purpose: The Faro landing headline (once) and its CRM analog, .stat-value's tabular-nums dashboard numerals.

body.purpose: Running text and the composer; the CRM's actual html{font-size} base.

label.purpose: Tracked-caps micro labels: stat labels, form labels, section headers, badge text.

shadows.name: elev-3
shadows.purpose: The one true offset shadow in the system, dark theme. Reserved for content that floats fully above the page: modal and global-search overlay only.

shadows.name: elev-3-light
shadows.purpose: Same overlay shadow, light theme — warm-tinted rather than blue-grey so it doesn't fight the sand accent.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve used across hover, focus and state transitions.

motion.name: dur-enter
motion.purpose: Entrance animation for panels and dropdowns.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one flat, solid two-tone chip. Inverts by theme: sand-on-charcoal dark, charcoal-on-warm-sand light. No tint, no gradient, no glow.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 7px 14px; background: #1A1A1A; color: #F4E7C8; border: none; border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.55), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(64,52,32,0.14); font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: filter 140ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-primary:active { filter: brightness(0.96); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #96742F; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.45; cursor: not-allowed; filter: none; }

components.name: Secondary (Icon) Button
components.description: The ghost icon button used everywhere a primary chip would be too loud — a near-transparent fill with a rim, tinting toward the accent on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; padding: 7px 14px; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #FAF6EE 0%, #FFFAF2 100%); border: 1px solid #D9CCB0; border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.70), inset 0 -1px 0 rgba(64,52,32,0.10); color: #6B6252; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: background 220ms, border-color 220ms, color 220ms; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: linear-gradient(180deg, rgba(232,215,177,0.16) 0%, rgba(232,215,177,0.09) 100%); border-color: rgba(232,215,177,0.32); color: #6E5320; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #96742F; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-secondary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Stat Card
components.description: The dashboard's core metric card: flat raised surface, tan edge, one-tone lift plus per-metric accent hairline on hover — never a resting shadow.
components.css: .ds-stat-card { position: relative; overflow: hidden; background: #FAF6EE; border: 1px solid #D9CCB0; border-radius: 12px; padding: 22px 20px 18px; transition: transform 220ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1), border-color 220ms; } .ds-stat-card:hover { transform: translateY(-2px); border-color: #E8D7B1; } .ds-stat-label { font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.8px; color: #6B6252; margin-bottom: 10px; } .ds-stat-value { font-family: 'Space Grotesk', 'Inter', sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; font-size: 28px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: #1F1D19; line-height: 1; }

components.name: Status Badge
components.description: Every status pairs colour with a translated text label — never colour alone. Pill shape, 10% tint fill, matching ink text.
components.css: .ds-badge { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 5px; padding: 4px 10px; border-radius: 20px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.2px; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-badge-yes { background: rgba(47,143,78,0.10); color: #226838; border: 1px solid rgba(47,143,78,0.22); } .ds-badge-no { background: rgba(194,53,43,0.10); color: #A52D25; border: 1px solid rgba(194,53,43,0.22); } .ds-badge-new { background: rgba(155,149,136,0.12); color: #504738; border: 1px solid rgba(155,149,136,0.2); }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Recessed field on the login stage: sits one step darker than its panel, focus adds an accent border plus a soft ring — the one intentional glow in the system.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 15px 18px; background: #FAF6EE; border: 1.5px solid #D9CCB0; border-radius: 12px; color: #1F1D19; font-size: 15px; font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; outline: none; transition: border-color 200ms, background-color 200ms, box-shadow 200ms; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: #E8D7B1; box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px rgba(232,215,177,0.25); } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #A2977F; }

components.name: Active Nav Item
components.description: The sidebar's one filled state — a solid sand pill with charcoal text and icon, no glow beneath it (an earlier accent glow under the active pill was explicitly removed).
components.css: .ds-nav-item { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 12px; padding: 11px 14px; border-radius: 10px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; color: #A79B85; cursor: pointer; } .ds-nav-item-active { background: #E8D7B1; color: #120F08; font-weight: 600; box-shadow: none; }

narrative.overview:
Helvaro is not a screen full of purple-AI gradients pretending to be intelligent, and it is not a cream editorial essay pretending to be a magazine. It is a warm sand board with real product pieces pinned to it in workflow order — the same material logic the marketing site uses (.impeccable/surfaces/site-index-html.md), inherited wholesale by the app rather than re-invented for it. Three tone steps carry the whole page (ground → raised → the third, darkest/lightest step), nothing lives between them, and a muted-tan edge does the work a shadow would do elsewhere. Depth is a lift of one tone step plus a border shifting toward the accent, not a diffuse glow underneath.

Sand (#E8D7B1) is the one brand accent and it is a fill, never type — the ratio on white is ~1.7:1, unreadable, which is why every accent-as-text use routes through a separately tuned ink variant (--accent-ink, --sand-on-surface). Charcoal and sand form the product's one deliberate two-tone chip, and which one is the fill flips by theme: dark reads sand-on-charcoal, light reads charcoal-on-warm-sand — same two colours, same solid block, inverted. Two structural exceptions to the single-accent rule are recorded, bounded, and contrast-checked rather than left implicit: Command Center's five category tones (hot/ready/risk/value/cold) and Faro's nine quick-action icon hues, each confined to one small chip and never touching text, borders or charts.

Two themes are peers, not an inversion of each other. Dark Helvaro is a warm near-black board under evening light, not a colour-flipped mirror of the light board; both were independently measured for contrast (all pairs ≥4.5:1 except the two exempted text-disabled pairs). Light is the shipped default. One surface deliberately does not follow either theme: the login podium and Faro's own canvas stay dark regardless of the app's theme, because they are a stage the brand performs on, not a workspace the user reads all day.
keyCharacteristics: Three tone steps per theme (ground / raised / third step), a tan edge instead of a shadow, and a one-step lift on hover/active — never a floating card.
Sand fills, an ink variant (measured per surface) carries it as text; the one two-tone chip (sand+charcoal) inverts by theme rather than existing as two different patterns.
Space Grotesk carries headings and the big tabular numerals; Inter carries everything a user actually reads.
Status is never colour-only: every badge, chip and status pill in the shipped markup pairs its colour with a translated text label.
The login podium and Faro's canvas are permanently dark, by name, as the one exception to "the app follows the theme."
Faro and Command Center run on an enforced closed scale (--sp-*, --r-*, --fs-*); the CRM dashboard surface — the majority of the shipped product — keeps its own parallel, unenforced rhythm.

rules.name: The Fill-Not-Type Rule
rules.body: Sand fills; it is never set as running text. Anywhere sand carries text, it routes through an -ink (or sand-on-surface) variant measured against the exact surface it sits on.

rules.name: The Inverted Chip Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one primary-button pattern in this system: a flat, solid two-tone chip, sand-on-charcoal or charcoal-on-warm-sand. Which colour is the fill inverts by theme; the pattern itself — solid block, no tint, no gradient — does not.

rules.name: The One-Accent Rule
rules.body: Sand is the only brand accent. Two bounded, named, contrast-verified exceptions exist and are not precedent for a third: Command Center's five semantic category tones and Faro's nine quick-action icon hues, each confined to a single small element. Every former per-card hue (--c-blue, --c-purple, --c-cyan, --c-gold) is now a legacy alias resolving back to sand.

rules.name: The Edge-Not-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth is a tan border plus a one-tone lift. A diffuse shadow under a resting card is the specific defect this system was rebuilt away from; --elev-3 is the sole, named exception, for true overlays only (modal, global search).

dos: Do fill with sand; carry it as text only through a per-surface -ink/sand-on-surface variant, never the raw accent hex.
Do lift a card or pill one tone step and/or shift its border toward the accent on hover — never add a shadow to a resting surface.
Do pair every status indicator with a translated text label, not colour alone.
Do keep the login podium and Faro's own canvas dark regardless of the app theme; let the CRM side follow [data-theme] as normal.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion on every custom animation.
Do route new Faro or Command Center CSS through --sp-*/--r-*/--fs-* — scripts/faro-check.js fails a raw px there.
Do measure a status colour's contrast against the actual tinted chip it renders on, not the bare card underneath.
donts: Don't use a gradient as a surface fill (card, panel, button). Known unrepaired exceptions — the light-theme .btn-icon and the .fm-btn-primary / .ap-btn-primary buttons — still ship one and are drift to fix, not a pattern to extend. A horizontal two-stop accent gradient for progress/meter fills is a separate, real, reused convention and not the same violation.

Don't add a glow (button, card, or text). --btn-glow/--shadow-glow are permanently none. Known unrepaired exception: .stat-value's colour variants and .analyse-stat-big still carry a text-shadow glow in dark mode.
Don't invent a second brand colour — every former per-card hue now aliases sand; the two bounded status/icon exceptions are not precedent for a third.
Don't call the product "AI" in customer-facing copy — describe what Faro/Helvaro does instead.
Don't set pure black or pure white as a surface or text colour.
Don't borrow the other surface's radius numbers — CRM buttons/cards are 8px/12px; Faro and Command Center are 14px/18px.
